primary_citation: Cal. Code Civ. Proc. §425.13 (Stats. 1987, Ch. 1498 (AB 3601), effective 1988-01-01)
short_title: Punitive Damages Gate — Professional Negligence Against Health Care Providers
one_line_rule: No punitive damages claim may be included in any pleading against a health care provider for professional negligence unless the court, on noticed motion supported by affidavit, finds substantial probability the plaintiff will prevail under §3294.

case_law.cite: Central Pathology Service Medical Clinic, Inc. v. Superior Court, 3 Cal.App.4th 181 (1992)
case_law.court: California Court of Appeal, Second Appellate District
case_law.key_rule: Substance-over-label: §425.13 applies if the claim arises out of professional negligence, regardless of how plaintiff labels the cause of action. Genuine independent intentional torts (no nexus to professional conduct) are exempt.

case_law.cite: College Hospital, Inc. v. Superior Court, 8 Cal.4th 704 (1994)
case_law.key_rule: 'Despicable' = so vile, base, contemptible, miserable, wretched or loathsome that it would be looked down upon and despised by ordinary decent people. 'Substantial probability' = prima facie case showing, not summary judgment standard. Financial motive + conscious disregard = despicable.

micra_lattice_position.gate_function: §425.13 is the procedural gate; must be cleared before punitive damages can be pled
micra_lattice_position.cap_interaction: §3333.2 caps noneconomic compensatory damages but does NOT cap punitive damages; clearing §425.13 unlocks uncapped punitive recovery
micra_lattice_position.collateral_source_interaction: §3333.1 affects compensatory side only; punitive damages are separate and unaffected
micra_lattice_position.hrimnak_escape: Genuine intentional tort framing removes claim from §425.13 scope entirely (Central Pathology substance-over-label test); if escape applies, §3333.2 cap and §6146 fee cap also fall

spine_surgery_fraud.theory: Surgeon performing clinically unindicated surgery for financial gain = conscious disregard of patient safety for financial benefit = despicable under College Hospital
evidence_package: Expert declaration: surgery not clinically indicated per pre-op findings
Billing records: procedure selected maximized reimbursement
Outcome evidence: post-surgical condition worse than pre-surgical
Prior Medical Board complaints if any: pattern = conscious disregard
Surgeon financial records (if obtainable): correlation between billing maximization and procedure selection
spine_surgery_fraud.dual_track_pleading: File intentional fraud/battery claim (Hrimnak escape attempt) + prepare §425.13 motion in parallel; if intentional tort survives, no gate; if Central Pathology catches it, §425.13 motion already ready

sirva_case.theory: §425.13 applies if claim is framed as professional negligence. Walgreens injector = health care provider scope question (verify on facts). Evidence: training records + prior SIRVA complaints at that location + injector technique documentation
sirva_case.note: SIRVA doctrine cross-referenced; health care provider status of pharmacy/pharmacist/technician must be verified on the specific facts
